To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have detected 11 gas-rich galaxies in z~1 clusters, finding that the cluster galaxies have high f_gas and long {\tau}, and that the cluster galaxies are consistent with the strong increase in the field gas fraction with redshift.

the gas fractions and depletion time-scales of gas-rich galaxies at z=1-2 in high-density environments are higher than their field counterparts, and that the gas fractions in cluster galaxies evolve similarly to their field counterparts, rising with redshift.

We detect molecular gas in 11 galaxies in 3 galaxy clusters at z~1, with average gas fractions and depletion time scales that are 62% and a factor of 1.6 higher than the field, respectively, and we find that the evolution of the molecular gas fraction of cluster galaxies mimics the strong rise with cosmic time of field star-forming galaxies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that environment plays in the buildup of massive galaxies at z>1.
the evolution of the molecular gas properties in galaxies residing in dense environments at z>1.

the study of galaxy evolution in clusters at high-redshift, using the Spitzer Adaptative Optics Deep Survey (SpARCs) as a tool to select the brightest cluster galaxies (BCGs), as well as the brightest cluster members (BCMs) at z~1-1.6.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the molecular gas content of cluster galaxies evolves similarly to that of the field.
the cluster environments at high-redshifts are gas-rich and conducive for star formation, and are likely to play an important role in the formation of massive galaxies.
gas-rich galaxies in z~1-2 clusters appear to have higher gas fractions than the field, with the caveat that our results are based on small samples.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the molecular gas reservoirs in z~1 clusters are more abundant than those of their coeval field counterparts, but their gas fractions and depletion time-scales are not as enhanced as previously thought.

the gas fractions and depletion time scales in our cluster galaxies at z=1 are significantly larger than those in the coeval field population, and that the gas fractions in cluster galaxies have increased by a factor of ~3 since z~2.
the gas reservoirs of z~1.7 cluster galaxies appear to be more gas-rich than their counterparts in the field at the same epoch.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gas-rich galaxies in dense environments have gas fractions and depletion time-scales that are higher than their field analogs at the same stellar masses and redshifts.

the molecular gas reservoirs in cluster galaxies at z>1 are more substantial than those in their field counterparts, and that the elevated gas fractions are likely a consequence of their high star formation rates.
cluster galaxies at z>1.5 have higher gas fractions and longer depletion timescales than their coeval field counterparts, and that the gas fraction in clusters rises rapidly with redshift.
